title: US v. Google ad-tech — parties' deadline to file one jointly proposed Final Judgment (E.D. Va.)
source: ECF: the court's own signed order, fetched and checksummed; the deadline is one arithmetic step on a clause the order states in its own words (2026-09-02 + 30 days = 2026-10-02), the 30-day joint-proposal clause of Judge Leonie M. Brinkema's 2026-09-02 remedies order in United States et al v. Google LLC, No. 1:23-cv-00108 (E.D. Va.). THE ORDER ITSELF WAS READ IN FULL ON 2026-09-15 and is now the source: ECF No. 1857, 2 pages, PageID# 116363-64, signed Brinkema 09/02/26, downloaded from CourtListener's RECAP mirror of the signed PDF (storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.vaed.533508/gov.uscourts.vaed.533508.1857.0_1.pdf, HTTP 200, 97,430 bytes, md5 ce42291aa18e47b6ba1029fd7cc71f39) and text-extracted. It reads verbatim: 'ORDERED that within 30 days of the date of this Order the parties meet and confer and file one jointly proposed Final Judgment, reflecting the decisions and modifications imposed in the accompanying Memorandum Opinion and resolving any still-disputed issues. If any provision remains unresolved, the parties must include their respective versions of that provision in the Final Judgment, labeled as to the proponent. No argument or explanation supporting the provision is to be included. The parties will be notified if further briefing or oral argument is needed.' A footnote adds that the parties must also provide chambers a Microsoft Word version. Entry 1858 of the same date is the sealed Memorandum Opinion. THE PREFIX WENT NEWS: -> EST: ON THE 2026-09-15 READ AND EST: -> ECF: ON 2026-09-20. The first move was a correction — NEWS: means 'press-reported, not primary-verified', which stopped being true the moment the signed PDF was fetched. The second is the promotion, and it waited on the schema rather than on evidence: until issue #3058 added ECF: there was no confirmed prefix for a federal court's own filed document, so the checksummed order could only be labelled as an estimate. The date is not a cadence projection — it is the outer bound the order itself fixes, 'within 30 days of the date of this Order', one deterministic step from the order's signature date, which is why it is ECF: rather than EST:. THE SINGLE-SOURCE RISK THE 2026-09-08 ENTRY RECORDED IS RETIRED — ppc.land is no longer the only carrier of the 30-day clause (relevantaudience.com 2026-09-04 and playwire.com 2026-09-08 both carry it, both fetched HTTP 200 on 2026-09-15), and more to the point the clause is now read from the court's own signed text. STATUS PROMOTED TO CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 BY THE TAXONOMY PR FOR ISSUE #3058, which added ECF: to the confirmed-prefix table in market-events-data.ts — the gap ftc-v-amazon-antitrust-trial-2027-03-29 and google-adtech-opinion-unseal-2026-09-16 also document, and the sibling of the exchange-holiday gap measured in issue #2552. Date doubt was never among the reasons it sat at estimate. No-self-confirm is not violated: that rule binds a discovering sweep's own proposal (.github/prompts/event-research.md), and the document here was read by a LATER pulse (2026-09-15) than the sweep that discovered the event (2026-09-08), promoted here by a third pass on the evidence the ledger already records. THE FALSIFIER IS THE DOCKET: a consent motion extending the 30-day clause, or any later entry moving the date, returns this to estimate — RECAP is a mirror, so 'absent from RECAP' is absence-from-mirror, not absence from the docket. Docket state read the same day: the newest entry is 1858 (2026-09-02); no redaction motion and no consent motion to extend the 30-day clause had been filed one day before the 09-16 redaction deadline, read with the caveat that RECAP is a mirror rather than PACER itself (ecf.vaed.uscourts.gov is login-gated). justice.gov's ATR case page (/atr/case/us-and-plaintiff-states-v-google-llc-2023) resolves HTTP 200 — the 2026-09-08 entry's 404 was a wrong path, not a block — but has not posted the 2026-09-02 order; its newest document is dated 2025-11-21. Re-verified at the primary 2026-09-15
notes: Canonical file written by this event's own initial research, 2026-09-08, from the one proposal that existed (proposals/google-adtech-final-judgment-2026-10-02.from-goog-2026-10-28-print.json, 2026-09-08); the proposal is now inert and left in place. THE PROPOSAL'S CENTRAL FRAMING IS CORRECTED HERE, and the correction is the finding: it filed this as 'the operative document of the ad-tech case … this document resolves the terms', and the sibling google-adtech-opinion-unseal-2026-09-16 ledger inherited that, calling 10-02 the document that binds and saying the terms land 10-02 regardless. Both are wrong on the same point. 2026-10-02 is the deadline to FILE A PROPOSAL; entry of judgment is a separate, later, undated act of the court. The base rate is the same defendant's own sibling case, one year earlier and measured this session: Judge Mehta's search-case remedies opinion landed 2025-09-02, the parties were ordered to propose a final judgment by 2025-09-10 — and Final Judgment was not ENTERED until 2025-12-05, 94 days after the opinion and 86 days after the proposal deadline, with a 95-page memorandum opinion resolving the parties' disputes because, in Mehta's own words, 'the parties continued to see eye-to-eye on little, even with the benefit of the Remedies Opinion.' A 'jointly proposed' judgment is aspirational; the modal 10-02 outcome is a filing that discloses disagreement. Tier `medium` is KEPT but its reason is REPLACED, because the price argument for it does not survive: on Yahoo daily closes computed this session, GOOG vs QQQ single-session excess was -0.19% on 2025-09-10 (the search case's proposed-judgment day — indistinguishable from nothing) and only +0.75% on 2025-12-05 (the day judgment was actually ENTERED), fully given back the next session (-2.18%, -1.43% over the two). The tier survives on CADENCE, not on magnitude: 10-02 sits two sessions inside the goog-2026-10-28-print D-20 run-up window (entry close 2026-09-30, counted in sessions), so the roster's one planned directional long would be open across it, and `medium`'s 7-day band buys pulses on ~09-15/09-22/09-29 that `low`'s 30-day band would not — at `low` there would be no further assessment before the date at all. 2026-10-02 is also JOBS DAY (jobs-2026-10-02, `confirmed`, 08:30 ET, high impact) with 34 tracked events in the +/-5-day corridor, so its tape is unattributable for the same structural reason 09-16's was (FOMC). One hypothesis was tested and killed rather than carried: a funding lapse forcing a DOJ extension motion cannot happen here — PL 119-103 was signed 2026-09-02 and funds agencies through 2026-12-11 (government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30). Nothing dated found in this session's sweep is untracked, so this event proposes no new calendar entry. | 2026-09-15 pulse (D-17): the order was read in full and the ledger's central framing correction is now confirmed from the primary rather than argued from press plus a cross-case analogy. Two things the press never carried. First, the order EXPRESSLY PRESCRIBES THE FORMAT FOR DISAGREEMENT — unresolved provisions carry both parties' versions 'labeled as to the proponent' with 'no argument or explanation', and 'the parties will be notified if further briefing or oral argument is needed'. So a 10-02 filing that discloses a dispute is the instrument working as written, not a deadline missed; and correspondingly FT-google-adtech-final-judgment-2026-10-02-1 is now a near-formality whose information value has dropped, recorded honestly in the ledger rather than by editing the append-only row. Second, a footnote requires an editable Microsoft Word copy to chambers, which together with the further-briefing clause STRENGTHENS the 'entry of judgment is a separate later act' leg (FT-...-2). The stance is UNCHANGED — stand aside on all four horizons — because it never rested on the filing being a surprise; it rests on the market not paying for paperwork, and the measured comparable is still -0.19%. Month-horizon confidence moved medium-high -> high. Tape since the last row: GOOG 335.38 -> 339.57, +3.12% excess vs QQQ on the week, reversing the post-ruling round-trip the 09-08 row flagged (now +2.65% excess vs the 09-01 pre-ruling close), but GOOG is the LAGGARD of its own complex over that stretch (META +15.35% excess, TTD +9.93%) and the one big session (09-14, +3.86% excess) is reported as dividend pay-date flow plus the Mechanize acquisition close, with TTD outrunning GOOG the same day — not the shape of an 'AdX stays' relief bid. Macro moved against clean attribution: August core CPI ran 0.3% m/m, +0.1pp above consensus (09-11), traders moved to price a hike at the 09-16 FOMC, and VIX went 15.26 -> 17.59, so 10-02's payroll tape is louder rather than quieter. The corridor grew from 34 to 51 tracked events within +/-5 days, four of them confirmed high-impact (pce-2026-09-30, ism-manufacturing-2026-10-01, jobs-2026-10-02, ism-services-2026-10-05), now recorded in the ledger's probe-ref adjacentStrongIds, which the previous block omitted entirely. No new dated adjacency found, so this event still proposes no new calendar entry: the docket sets no hearing or entry date, ATR lists nothing forward, and entry of judgment plus the Fourth Circuit notice remain undated by construction.
